stories.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
stories.body: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president called an "utterly horrific" attack.

stories.title: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace
stories.body: Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in any offensive operations.

stories.title: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators
stories.body: The National Transportation Safety Board also believes weather could have been a factor in the crash, but warns it is too early to determine the cause.

stories.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
stories.body: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.

stories.title: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
stories.body: Though unprecedented, the six-day truce has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that continues to grinds on.

stories.title: Legal challenge to Australia's social media ban to start in High Court
stories.body: A rights group will argue the world-leading policy robs under-16s of their right to free communication.

stories.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
stories.body: US government agencies and cyber analysts have blamed Pyongyang for the record-breaking heist.

stories.title: Man and boy arrested after allegedly attacking One Nation volunteer with baseball bat in Australia
stories.body: The incident comes amid growing calls for the temperature of political debate in Australia to be turned down.

stories.title: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
stories.body: The case, part of the "Farmgate" scandal, has left President Cyril Ramaphosa mired in an impeachment saga.

stories.title: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
stories.body: Jos Leijdekkers has been found guilty in absentia of cocaine smuggling and is believed to be in Sierra Leone.

stories.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
stories.body: The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by the US Treasury.

stories.title: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
stories.body: Many Ukrainians, who have faced years of Russian attacks, did not take the messages seriously and doubted their veracity.

stories.title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
stories.body: The attack on Donovan Marx, 50, comes as right-wing groups say there is a genocide of white people - a claim widely discredited.

stories.title: Wizz Air flight from Luton in emergency landing after bomb threat
stories.body: A Hungarian fighter jet escorted the aircraft to Budapest after the threat was received mid-air.

stories.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
stories.body: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.

stories.title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
stories.body: Uganda has been helping Somalia battle an insurgency led by the al-Shabab militant group since 2007.

stories.title: China state broadcaster pulls La Liga matches following Mbappé joke
stories.body: China Media Group, which acknowledged Mbappé's apology, has not said how long the blackout will last.

stories.title: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
stories.body: There were hundreds of arrests as protesters took to the streets in cities across France for the third weekend in a row.

stories.title: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
stories.body: The author of Jasper Jones and Runt pleaded guilty in May after police raided his home months earlier.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
stories.body: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.

Meanwhile, European troop exercises in Ukraine indicate a forward-looking posture that balances readiness with peace-building aspirations. These signals collectively suggest a slow but deliberate pivot toward stability-seeking governance.

Looking ahead, **watch for concrete follow-through on governance-oriented initiatives.** Key indicators include the Dutch police's ability to leverage the €2 million reward effectively, further developments in European troop exercises, and Uganda's domestic policy shifts post-withdrawal.
